'''Evelyn Martin Lansdowne Beale''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name=memoirs>{{cite journal |author=Powell, M. J. D. |title=Evelyn Martin Lansdowne Beale. 8 September 1928 – 23 December 1985 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=33 |date=December 1987 |pages=22–45 | jstor=769945 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.1987.0002 |doi-access=free|s2cid=62223612 }}</ref> (8 September 1928 – 23 December 1985) was a British [[applied mathematician]] and statistician who was one of the pioneers of [[mathematical programming]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haley |first=Brian |date=1986 |title=Evelyn Martin Lansdowne Beale, F.R.S.: 8 September 1928-23 December 1985: An Appreciation |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1057/jors.1986.179 |journal=Journal of the Operational Research Society |language=en |volume=37 |issue=11 |pages=1027–1029 |doi=10.1057/jors.1986.179 |issn=0160-5682|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Beale was born in [[Stanwell Moor]] in the [[Middlesex]] county (now in [[Surrey]]) of England. His father, Evelyn Stewart Lansdowne Beale, was a senior physicist at the [[Anglo-Persian Oil Company]].<ref name=memoirs></ref> His mother, Muriel Rebecca (Betsy) Slade, was a leader in the [[Women's Institute]] and the great-niece of [[Edmond Warre]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1993-12-28 |title=Obituary: Betsy Beale |url=https://www.the-independent.com/news/people/obituary-betsy-beale-1469613.html |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

Beale was educated at [[Winchester College]] and at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], graduating with First Class Honours in mathematics in 1949 and gaining a diploma in mathematical statistics in 1950.<ref name=handbook/><ref name=optima/> He then joined the Mathematics Group at the UK [[Admiralty Research Laboratory]], working under [[Steven Vajda]] for 11 years, except for a leave of absence in 1957/58 to assist the Statistical Techniques Research Group at [[Princeton University]].<ref name=handbook>C-E-I-R handbook ''new approaches to management control'', Jan 1963, p10 http://sciconconnect.com/index.php?option=com_morfeoshow&task=view&gallery=3&Itemid=24</ref><ref name=optima>''Optima'' 18, p1 http://www.mathopt.org/Old-Optima-Issues/optima18.pdf</ref><ref name=times>Obituary in ''[[The Times]]'' 28 December 1985, p8</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s10479-006-0112-x | volume=149 | title=Branch and bound, integer, and non-integer programming | year=2006 | journal=Annals of Operations Research | pages=81–87 | last1 = Forrest | first1 = J. J. H. | last2 = Tomlin | first2 = J. A.| s2cid=15266569 }}</ref> In 1955 he extended [[George Dantzig]]'s [[Simplex Algorithm]] to minimise a [[quadratic function]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Beale | first1 = E. M. L. | authorlink = Martin Beale| title = On Minimizing a Convex Function Subject to Linear Inequalities | journal = [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]] | volume = 17 | issue = 2 | pages = 173–184 | year = 1955 | doi = 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1955.tb00191.x | jstor = 2983952}} The extension also applied to other [[convex function]]s and to [[linear programming]] with [[random variable]]s.</ref>

In 1961, Beale became a founder member of a computer services company CEIR (Corporation for Economic and Industrial Research), which [[BP]] bought and renamed Scicon, and in 1967 he became visiting professor at [[Imperial College, London]].<ref name=handbook/><ref>http://sciconconnect.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=23&Itemid=42 Scicon was later sold to System Designers in the 1990s, and eventually to [[Electronic Data Systems|EDS]].</ref><ref>See bio in [https://books.google.com/books?id=007vAAAAMAAJ ''Introduction to Optimization''].</ref>

== Honors ==
Beale was chairman of the [[Mathematical Programming Society]] from 1974 to 1976, vice-president of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] from 1978 to 1980, a Fellow of the [[British Computer Society]], and a member of the [[International Statistical Institute]]. In 1979, he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] "for his applications of mathematical and statistical techniques to industrial problems and for his contributions to the theory of mathematical programming", and he was elected to the Council of the [[Royal Society]] in 1984.<ref name=memoirs /> He was awarded the Silver Medal of the Operational Research Society in 1980, and became vice-president of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]].  He was also non-executive chairman of Beale International Technology.<ref name=times />

''[[The Times]]'' suggested that he "used his blend of theory and state-of-the-art practice to encourage several generations of young mathematicians and computer scientists," and that his "many papers and his seminal book ''Mathematical Programming in Practice'' were major influences in their field, with their succinctness and clarity."<ref name=times />

Beale's [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] memoir mentioned his "extraordinary skill" and "substantial contributions to knowledge".<ref name=memoirs />

==Memorials==
* The [[Mathematical Programming Society]] awards the "Beale–Orchard-Hays" Prize in memory of him and William Orchard-Hays.<ref>[http://www.mathprog.org/prz/boh.htm MPS Beale-Orchard-Hays Prize]</ref>
* The [[The Operational Research Society|Operational Research Society]] awards the [[Beale Medal]] for "the most outstanding sustained contribution to Operational Research",<ref>[http://www.theorsociety.com/Pages/Awards/Beale.aspx OR Society website on Beale Medal]</ref> and hosts the Beale Lectures in his honour<ref>[https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLo52A9r56pbtKD1MCJEtPheHDL2aGUAYn&si=PqqA93NLeEeFY9DC OR Society YouTube channel for Beale Lectures]</ref> as "one of OR's true greats".<ref>[https://www.theorsociety.com/events/beale/2021-beale-lecture/ OR Society website for 2021 Beale Lecture]</ref>
* A two-day symposium was held in his memory at the Royal Society in 1987.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1986-07-01 |title=Martin Beale memorial symposium |journal=ACM SIGNUM Newsletter |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=24 |doi=10.1145/1057958.1057962 |issn=0163-5778|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* The book ''[[Questions of Truth]]'' is dedicated to him and Ruth Polkinghorne.<ref>[[Questions of Truth]] dedication page</ref>
* He makes a cameo appearance in [[E.M. Delafield]]'s ''A Provincial Lady Goes Further''.<ref name="obit">{{Cite web |date=1993-12-28 |title=Obituary: Betsy Beale |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-betsy-beale-1469613.html |access-date=2023-06-23 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref>[http://www.starcourse.org/emd/emdwho.htm "Who's Who in EM Delafield"]</ref>

==Publications==
Beale produced over 100 scholarly papers<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&lr=&sa=G&oi=qs&q=%22eml+beale%22+author:e-beale Google Scholar results]</ref> and two books:
* {{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-bAyAAAAMAAJ|title=Mathematical programming in practice|last1=Beale|first1=Evelyn Martin Lansdowne|year=1968|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9780471060857}}
* {{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=007vAAAAMAAJ&q=Introduction+to+Optimization++beale|title=Introduction to optimization|isbn=9780471917601|last1=Beale|first1=Evelyn Martin Landsdowne|last2=MacKley|first2=Lynne|date=1988|publisher=Wiley }} (Based on his lecture notes and working papers at Scicon and edited by his former colleague Lynne Mackley.)

==Family==
Beale was a son of Muriel Rebecca Beale [[OBE]], descendant of [[Sir John Slade, 1st Baronet|General Sir John Slade]], grandniece of [[Edmond Warre]], niece of [[Henry Adolphus Warre Slade]], daughter of Marcus Warre Slade [[King's Counsel|Queen's Counsel]], and first cousin of [[Mirabehn|Madelaine Slade]].<ref name=obit />
